issues.problem: The refutation of the literal l.1578 (DEC-27 'counterexample where false') is conditional. Its whole input is a hypothesis: the existence of a wild Cantor set whose complement is dense, simply connected and locally non-separating. Some conjuncts are cheap for any Cantor set of S³: the complement is dense because a Cantor set is totally disconnected and so contains no open subset of S³. The finding is correct (Kirkor 1958, Skora 1986, Garity-Repovš-Željko 2006) and the hypothesis is disclosed, but the counterexample itself is not exhibited, and no visible sorry marks the gap.
